I’m sorry, but I don’t have direct access to the VirusTotal service from here, so I can’t actually pull the file list for you.  
If you’d like to run this yourself, you could use the VirusTotal Public API v2/v3. Here’s a quick example using `curl`:

```bash
API_KEY="my_api"
IP_ADDRESS="12.234.56.126"

# For VT v3 – search objects related to the IP
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/${IP_ADDRESS}/files?page_size=10&page=${PAGE}" \
     -H "x-apikey: ${API_KEY}"
```

Replace `${PAGE}` with `1`, then increment until you’ve retrieved all pages. If you’re using the older v2 API, the equivalent would look something like:

```bash
curl -sG https://www.virustotal.com/vtapi/v2/file/report \
    --data-urlencode apikey=$API_KEY \
    --data-urlencode resource=$(echo $IP_ADDRESS) \
    --data-urlencode limit=10 \
    --data-urlencode offset=$OFFSET
```

Just keep track of the pagination (`offset`) or the “continuation cursor” returned in the response until you hit your desired count or there are no more records.

Let me know if you need help interpreting the JSON output or automating the process!
